title: String bean Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: String bean Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: String bean nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen and phosphorus in sitaw, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: String bean nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your sitaw (string bean) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, magnesium, boron and manganese. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and magnesium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But boron and manganese stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which string bean nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a string bean nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest string bean nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in string bean

Lower leaves turn pale and yellow and the vines climb slowly with light green leaves and few pods. Sitaw fixes its own nitrogen through root nodules, so this usually means poor nodulation. You see it most at this stage: three to six weeks after planting, before heavy flowering.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in sitaw

In a legume this usually means poor nodulation: no inoculant in a field new to the crop, inoculant killed by sun or heat, very acid soil, waterlogging, hot dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer near the seed, which stops nodules from forming.
How to tell it apart

Sulfur deficiency yellows the young leaves first. Iron and manganese deficiency yellow between green veins on young leaves. To be sure, dig, do not pull, a few plants 3 to 6 weeks after planting, wash the roots and cut some nodules open. Pink to red inside means they are working, white means not active yet, and brown, grey or mushy means dead.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency
Feed the crop now with a light sidedress of Urea 46 0 0 or Complete 14 14 14 beside the plants, following the soil test, since new nodules cannot be added to a standing crop (Texas AandM).

Phosphorus deficiency in string bean
Vines grow slowly and stay short, with dark or bluish green leaves and few flowers and pods. Roots and nodules are small. You see it most at this stage: seedling to first harvest.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in sitaw
Acid soils and soils low in phosphorus. UF IFAS gives pH 5.5 to 6.5 as best for long bean.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen deficiency makes leaves pale, not dark. To be sure, soil test for phosphorus before planting.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency
Apply 16 20 0 or Complete 14 14 14 at planting, following the soil test. For a standing crop TNAU gives a 2 percent DAP 18 46 0 spray (20 g per liter) every 15 days for pulses.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, mix phosphorus and compost into the planting holes or rows each season.
Potassium deficiency in string bean

The tips and edges of older leaflets turn yellow, the yellow spreads toward the center. The edges die and brown before the leaves drop. Sitaw is the same species as cowpea, so the signs match. Pods stay short and thin. You see it most at this stage: flowering and the long harvest period.
Why potassium deficiency happens in sitaw
Sandy soils, long picking seasons that take a lot of potassium away, and no potash in the program.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium deficiency yellows between the veins of old leaves, not the edges. To be sure, soil test for potassium.
What to apply for potassium deficiency
Sidedress Muriate of potash 0 0 60 or Complete 14 14 14 following the soil test. TNAU gives a 1 percent potassium chloride spray (10 g per liter) for cowpea type beans.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, feed potash again during the picking season on sandy soils.
Magnesium deficiency in string bean

Areas between the veins of older leaves turn yellow, then deep yellow with rusty specks and dead blotches. Sitaw is the same species as cowpea, so the signs match. You see it most at this stage: mid season, during heavy picking.
Why magnesium deficiency happens in sitaw
Acid sandy soils and heavy potash use.
How to tell it apart
Potassium deficiency starts at leaf edges and tips. To be sure, soil test for magnesium and pH.
What to apply for magnesium deficiency
TNAU gives a 1 percent magnesium sulfate spray (10 g Epsom salt per liter) every 15 days for cowpea. Use Dolomite on acid soils as the soil test advises.

Sold here with magnesium: **Dolomite** by A6 Agrisource Limited Corporation (24 percent calcium and 11 percent magnesium), **YaraTera KRISTA MgS** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (16 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur), **Magnepro** by Ramgo International Corporation (16 percent MgO and 12.8 percent sulfur) and **Lucky Planters Magnesium Sulphate Heptahydrate (Epsom Salt)** by Mindanao Agriplus Corporation (16.27 percent MgO and 13 percent sulfur). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [complete fertilizer](/blog/complete-fertilizer-14-14-14), and the page on [magnesium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/magnesium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, lime acid soils with dolomite before planting.
Boron deficiency in string bean
Young leaves crinkle and stay small, and the vine top grows poorly. Sitaw is the same species as cowpea, so the signs match. You see it most at this stage: flowering and pod set.
Why boron deficiency happens in sitaw
Sandy soils low in organic matter, high pH soils and dry spells.
How to tell it apart
Virus diseases crinkle leaves too, but with a yellow and green mosaic. To be sure, leaf or soil test for boron.
What to apply for boron deficiency
TNAU gives a 0.2 percent borax spray (2 g per liter) for cowpea. Keep boron out of the seed row (UW).

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, add compost and water evenly at flowering.
Manganese deficiency in string bean

Leaves turn pale green to yellow between green veins, starting on the young leaves, with brown spots later. Sitaw is the same species as cowpea, so the signs match. You see it most at this stage: early growth.
Why manganese deficiency happens in sitaw
High pH, over limed sandy soils and soils high in organic matter. Beans need much manganese (UW).
How to tell it apart
Iron deficiency turns the veins yellow too. To be sure, leaf test and soil pH.
What to apply for manganese deficiency
TNAU gives 5 kg manganese sulfate per hectare to the soil or two sprays 10 days apart for cowpea. The University of Wisconsin gives about 1.1 kg of manganese per hectare as a spray for beans.

(12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [manganese deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/manganese-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, do not lime beyond pH 6.5.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any string bean nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories and the Bureau of Soils and Water Management test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your sitaw needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: String bean nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my sitaw leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: vines grow weak and light green, lower leaves yellow, and the roots have few working nodules. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at manganese deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in string bean?
items.a: Feed the crop now with a light sidedress of Urea 46 0 0 or Complete 14 14 14 beside the plants, following the soil test, since new nodules cannot be added to a standing crop (Texas AandM).

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in string bean?
items.a: Apply 16 20 0 or Complete 14 14 14 at planting, following the soil test. For a standing crop TNAU gives a 2 percent DAP 18 46 0 spray (20 g per liter) every 15 days for pulses.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in string bean?
items.a: Sidedress Muriate of potash 0 0 60 or Complete 14 14 14 following the soil test. TNAU gives a 1 percent potassium chloride spray (10 g per liter) for cowpea type beans.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my sitaw lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the string bean nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
